Financed extras (such as insurance added to the loan) raise the EMI but not the money received
Offers are ranked by APR: the rate at which the EMIs repay the loan less its fees

values.label: Months for the saving to cover the cost

steps: Both EMIs are worked out on the same balance and the same months left
Monthly rate i = 1%; each month the SIP is added and grows by (1 + i)
The SIP rises at the start of each year by the step-up
Goal in future money = today's cost × (1 + inflation)^years
SIP needed = (goal − savings grown) ÷ what a SIP of 1 grows to
Each month: take the withdrawal at the start, then the rest grows a month
The withdrawal rises at the start of each year by the increase

values.label: Monthly expense in the first month of retirement
What you have, grown to retirement

steps: Expense at retirement = today's expense × (1 + inflation)^years to retirement
Corpus = the present value at retirement of monthly expenses rising with inflation and paid at the start of each month, discounted at the return after retirement
Cumulative: P × (1 + r/n)^(n × years); under six months: P × (1 + r × years)
Each instalment grows quarterly for the months it stays: R × (1 + r/4)^(months left / 3)
Deposited by 5 April each year, so it earns the full year; interest is compounded yearly
Deposits for the first 15 years; interest compounds yearly until year 21
Each month: employee + employer EPF share is added; interest = Σ monthly balances × rate / 12, credited at the year end (as EPFO works it)

values.label: Lump sum you can take (tax-free up to 60%)

steps: Pension = corpus × annuity share × annuity rate ÷ 12 (a level annuity for life)

Term plan + mutual fund: the fund at the end
Term plan + mutual fund minus ULIP

steps: Each year the premium less the allocation charge goes in; each month admin and mortality charges come out, the fund grows, and the fund management charge is taken
Comparison: the same premium, less a term plan's premium, in a mutual fund earning the same gross return less its expense ratio

values.label: Buyer's wealth: home value − loan left (+ savings invested)
Renter's wealth: the down payment and savings invested

steps: Each month the cheaper side invests the difference between owning (EMI + maintenance) and rent
The renter starts by investing the down payment and purchase costs

steps: SLN = (cost − salvage) / life

values.label: Interest as a share of the loan

steps: EMI = P · i / (1 − (1 + i)^−n), i = annual rate / 12
Each month: interest = balance × i; principal = EMI − interest
Each month: take the withdrawal at the start, then the rest grows a month
The withdrawal rises at the start of each year by the increase

Rate from the salvage value: 1 − (salvage / cost)^(1/life) = 45.072%
WDV = book value at the start of the year × rate

Terminal value's share of the total

steps: Value = Σ FCFₜ / (1 + r)^t + TV / (1 + r)^N
TV by growth = FCF_N (1 + g) / (r − g); by multiple = multiple × the metric at year N
WACC = E/V·Ke + D/V·Kd(1 − t) + P/V·Kp
Ke by CAPM = Rf + β × market risk premium
ROE = margin × turnover × equity multiplier
Five-step: ROE = (NI/EBT)(EBT/EBIT)(EBIT/sales)(sales/assets)(assets/equity)

values.label: Justified trailing P/E: payout (1 + g) / (r − g)
